papers.title: The "I Don't Know" Filter: Enhancing Agentic Reliability in Function Calling

summary.tldr: A lightweight, trainable filter is proposed to quantify language model uncertainty and suppress potentially harmful, uncertain function calls, enhancing agentic reliability without modifying the base model.
key_points: Current language model evaluation metrics encourage positive claims even when uncertain, leading to hallucinations in function calling.
A new agent evaluation metric is proposed to account for negative outcomes of incorrect function calls.
A lightweight, trainable filter is introduced to detect and suppress uncertain function calls, preventing hallucinations.
The filter operates without modifying the underlying language model, offering a practical path to more reliable agents.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables agents to identify and avoid uncertain function calls, crucial for reliable deployment in high-stakes applications.

papers.title: Separating Representation from Reconstruction Enables Scalable Text Encoders

summary.tldr: CrossBERT, a two-part architecture, separates representation learning from token reconstruction, enabling scalable text encoders with improved throughput and sample efficiency.
key_points: BERT encoders' representations become unexploitable by frozen probes despite improved perplexity due to coupling representation learning with token reconstruction.
CrossBERT separates high-quality encoded representation learning from token reconstruction grounding.
CrossBERT uses a Complementary Masking Strategy, allowing high masking ratios (>=50%) and gradient collection over all tokens.
CrossBERT increases throughput by 1.5 to 2x and sample efficiency by 2x.
CrossBERT demonstrates superior performance on MTEB(eng, v2) and frozen GLUE benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This new architecture allows for more efficient and scalable text encoders, improving performance on downstream tasks.

papers.title: Full Glyph Images Beat Token Embeddings: A Controlled Study for Transformers

summary.tldr: A controlled study shows rasterized glyph images processed by a vision encoder outperform discrete token embeddings for Chinese language modeling in Transformers.
key_points: Replaced index-based token embeddings with a single rasterized image of the character sequence for Chinese language modeling.
Vision-based model, using a ResNet and shallow Vision Transformer, achieved 0.429 accuracy, a 21% relative improvement over the 0.355 baseline with index-based embeddings.
Vision model converged in approximately half the training epochs and maintained performance under moderate character corruption, matching the clean index-based baseline.
Advantage requires spatially coherent input and a ViT encoder with 2D positional encodings; it does not transfer to alphabetic systems like English.
summary.why_it_matters: This suggests that discrete tokenization is not a fundamental requirement for Chinese language modeling and Transformers are more modality-agnostic than commonly assumed.

papers.title: Probe, Don't Prompt: A Hidden-State Probe for Metadata Filtering in Multi-Meta-RAG

summary.tldr: A hidden-state probe replaces GPT-3.5 for metadata filtering in Multi-Meta-RAG, achieving 90.9% accuracy on MultiHop-RAG queries, outperforming GPT-3.5 and a substring baseline.
key_points: The probe achieves 90.9% set-exact accuracy on 2556 MultiHop-RAG queries, compared to 88.0% for a substring baseline and 80.9% for GPT-3.5.
The accuracy margin over GPT-3.5 is primarily due to the probe's handling of null queries, where GPT-3.5 never abstains.
The probe's output space is fixed to a 49-source vocabulary, preventing drift outside an allow-list.
Key design choices include selecting a shallow layer, mean pooling, and class-imbalance-aware multi-label training.
A 135M-parameter model performs within ~1.5 points of a 1.5B model, indicating low computational cost for the filter.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more accurate, deterministic, and cost-effective solution for metadata filtering in multi-hop question answering without relying on proprietary APIs.

papers.title: ReCoLoRA: Spectrum-Aware Recursive Consolidation for Continual LLM Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: ReCoLoRA introduces spectrum-aware recursive consolidation for continual LLM fine-tuning, outperforming existing LoRA-style methods on GLUE benchmarks by re-decomposing effective weights.
key_points: Adapters are initialized from a randomized SVD of the pretrained weight.
Per-layer effective ranks are selected using an elbow criterion.
Before each new task, ReCoLoRA re-decomposes the current effective weight into a frozen residual, a slowly updated principal component, and a fresh adapter.
ReCoLoRA achieved the best final average score on three of four 7-8B backbones on a six-task continual GLUE sequence against rank-swept LoRA, PiSSA, AdaLoRA, and DoRA baselines.
ReCoLoRA trains fewer parameters compared to the baselines while achieving superior performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves continual fine-tuning efficiency and performance for LLMs by mitigating catastrophic forgetting without increasing parameter count.

papers.title: Uncertainty-gated selection for block-sparse attention

summary.tldr: A value-of-information router improves block-sparse attention recall by adaptively expanding the kept set for queries with uncertain top-k block selection, achieving significant gains over static top-k.
key_points: The proposed router measures the decisiveness of the top-k cut for each query.
It doubles the kept set of blocks for queries where the score gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th blocks is smallest.
On LongBench-v2 medium, router-on-Quest achieved 0.75 paired recall, a +28 pp increase over top-k's 0.47.
The method preserves 0.81 and 0.89 of dense accuracy on Qwen2.5-7B-1M and Qwen3.6 at 128K context, with 0.62x and 0.80x dense wall time respectively.
The lift reproduces across Qwen2.5, Mistral-Nemo, and Qwen3.6 architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves the accuracy of block-sparse attention in long-context language models while maintaining computational efficiency.

papers.title: AdaptiveSD A Stability-Aware, Runtime-Adaptive Speculative Decoding Framework with Multi-Policy Orchestration for CPU-Constrained LLM Inference

summary.tldr: AdaptiveSD is a runtime-adaptive speculative decoding framework with multi-policy orchestration for CPU-constrained LLM inference, addressing performance degradation from bandwidth saturation and instability.
key_points: AdaptiveSD employs a Runtime Monitoring Engine to track computation signals.
An Adaptive Draft Controller enforces an eleven-rule policy hierarchy prioritizing system resource preservation.
A Dynamic Policy Engine uses heuristic and reinforcement learning to modify policies based on workload behavior.
A KV Cache Coordination Layer manages cache states with INT8 shadow buffers and position-aware evictions.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework aims to ensure robust and reliable execution of small quantized GGUF-based language models on CPU-constrained devices, preventing performance degradation and system failures.

papers.title: SABLE: An NDA-Safe Closed-Loop LLM Framework for Analog Circuit Optimization in Industrial EDA Flows

summary.tldr: SABLE is an NDA-safe closed-loop LLM framework enabling LLMs to optimize analog circuits within industrial EDA flows by scrubbing proprietary data and providing sanitized feedback.
key_points: SABLE employs an explicit threat model, a whitelist of 28 scoped SKILL entry points, and PDK/path/model scrubbing on every return path to ensure NDA safety.
The framework uses a strict JSON action contract with six machine-checked stop conditions and preserves best-so-far state.
Evaluated 11 LLM checkpoints on a 20 GHz LC-VCO tuning-curve task (7/11 models passed) and a two-stage op-amp task (4/11 models passed within 15 iterations).
Feedback-path ablations demonstrated that removing individual sanitized channels weakens specifications or degrades search performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework allows LLMs to be integrated into sensitive industrial analog circuit design processes without exposing proprietary or confidential information.

papers.title: CrossHallu: Do Hallucination Signals Generalize Across Languages and Domains in Large Language Model's Internals?

summary.tldr: CrossHallu evaluates the cross-lingual and cross-domain generalization of internal-state hallucination detection in six LLMs using generative question-answering, finding signals transfer across languages and domains.
key_points: CrossHallu is the first study to evaluate cross-lingual and cross-domain generalization of hallucination detection using LLM internal representations.
The study used six LLMs on a generative question-answering task with TruthfulQA, an Arabic translated TruthfulQA, and HalluScore.
Evaluation included monolingual, cross-lingual, cross-domain, and combined cross-lingual and cross-domain transfer scenarios.
Internal-state hallucination signals transferred across languages and domains for most models.
Cross-lingual performance depended on class separability and language alignment in the feature space, while cross-domain transfer in Arabic varied by training/testing datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This research indicates that hallucination detection methods based on internal LLM states can be generalized beyond English, enabling broader application.

papers.title: Can Dialects Be Steered Like Languages? Sparse Neurons and Distributed Directions in Arabic LLMs

summary.tldr: This study identifies sparse neurons and distributed directions in Arabic LLMs to steer dialectal generation without fine-tuning, addressing data scarcity for Arabic dialects.
key_points: Arabic LLMs overproduce Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) due to dialectal data scarcity, hindering dialectally accurate generation.
Neuron-level analysis identifies sparse neuron populations encoding dialect-specific features; amplifying or suppressing these neurons steers outputs toward target dialects.
A vector-steering approach extracts and injects dialect-specific activation directions during inference, addressing entangled dialectal features at the single-neuron level.
These methods provide interpretability probes and control mechanisms for dialect generation without requiring dialect-specific fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: This research offers a method to improve dialectal accuracy in Arabic LLMs at inference time, bypassing the need for extensive dialect-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: A Failure-Mode Benchmark for Polymorphic Sybil Poisoning in RAG

summary.tldr: A new benchmark and evaluation framework for RAG under coordinated retrieval poisoning introduces polymorphic sybil poisoning, revealing significant hijack amplification and detailed failure modes beyond traditional attack success rates.
key_points: Introduces "polymorphic sybil poisoning," a coordinated attack using S lexically diverse passages to support an attacker-chosen target, evading lexical near-duplicate filters.
Polymorphic sybil poisoning amplifies hijack by +18.8pp (95% CI [+15.4, +22.4]) compared to monomorphic copies, a 5.7x amplification of the ASR-visible attack channel.
The evaluation framework partitions reader outputs into four categories: gold, hijack, abstention, and drift, providing instance-level paired clean-to-poison transition matrices.
Abstention and drift together account for 47-66% of output mass under attack, representing failure profiles invisible to ASR+ACC metrics.
The benchmark includes 3,145 questions, 2,982 retained sybil groups (S=6), and is evaluated across five readers (7B-120B), two retrievers, and two datasets (TriviaQA, 2Wiki).
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a more granular understanding of RAG system vulnerabilities to sophisticated poisoning attacks, highlighting limitations of current evaluation metrics and enabling development of more robust defenses.

papers.title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Causality Assessment in Pharmacovigilance: Developing a Performance Metric as Objective for Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization

summary.tldr: A novel Gaussian Process-compatible metric, EWACS, was developed to optimize LLM temperature for improved causality assessment in pharmacovigilance, yielding significant agreement gains.
key_points: Four composite metrics (WCS, IWAS, EWACS, CWCS) were developed for Bayesian optimization of LLM performance on Naranjo causality assessment.
OpenAI's GPT-5.2 with Chain-of-Thought prompting achieved baseline agreement of 74.1% on Naranjo question 5 and 65.4% on question 10.
EWACS-guided Bayesian optimization improved causality classification agreement from 45.0% to 72.0% (+27 pp), with a 42.9 pp gain in 'Doubtful' cases.
Temperature optimization did not show a systematic population-level effect (eta = 0.002, p = 0.959), but case-specific temperature selection improved performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing LLM hyperparameters like temperature using metrics like EWACS can significantly enhance automated pharmacovigilance, improving the accuracy of causality assessments.

papers.title: PathMark: Protecting Intellectual Property of Mixture-of-Expert LLMs via Path Watermarks

summary.tldr: PathMark is the first watermarking framework for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, steering routing as a covert watermark channel to protect intellectual property against architectural mismatches and vulnerabilities.
key_points: PathMark addresses fragile decision boundaries and routing entanglement in MoE watermarking by actively steering routing through predetermined expert subsets.
It employs a distribution alignment loss to elevate target expert probabilities, a wide-path configuration for robustness, and a contrastive loss to prevent gradient leakage.
PathMark supports multi-bit encoding via combinatorial paths and offers both white-box routing inspection and black-box output detection for verification.
Experiments on four MoE models show >99% verification accuracy with <2% perplexity degradation, maintaining robustness against quantization, fine-tuning, pruning, and adaptive attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: PathMark enables intellectual property protection for high-value MoE LLMs, which was previously unachievable with existing watermarking techniques.

papers.title: Reward-Gated On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: RG-OPD introduces reward-gated on-policy distillation, using verifier feedback to selectively trust teacher logits, improving student performance in reasoning and coding tasks.
key_points: RG-OPD addresses unreliable teacher supervision in on-policy distillation by incorporating verifier feedback to determine when to trust teacher logits.
The method bridges sparse verifier rewards with dense teacher logits, maintaining token-level supervision while filtering misleading teacher signals.
RG-OPD improves over vanilla reverse-KL distillation by 2.9 points and TSD-KD by 4.9 points at 1K generation length.
In long-generation settings, RG-OPD improves over the untuned student by 8.2 points.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more effective transfer of reasoning abilities from large teacher models to smaller student models, leading to stronger distilled students.

papers.title: Scalable Semantic Steering of Embedding Projections

summary.tldr: A new scalable semantic steering method for embedding projections uses group-level LLM reasoning to reduce computational cost while maintaining alignment with analyst-defined semantic relationships.
key_points: The method shifts semantic computation from individual items to user-defined groups, using a single LLM call to generate structured profiles for all groups.
Hybrid semantic prototypes are formed by embedding group profiles and combining them with seed centroids.
Intent propagation occurs without retraining, using embedding-space soft assignment, abstention, and alignment-scaled updates before reprojection.
On a 5K-document LitCovid corpus, the method reduced LLM calls by over three orders of magnitude compared to per-item LLM steering, achieving comparable global alignment.
The prototype-based mechanism is demonstrated to extend to multimodal embeddings via an image case study.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach makes semantic steering more practical and cost-effective for larger embedding collections by significantly reducing LLM calls.

papers.title: Refused in Chat, Written in Code: Workflow-Level Jailbreak Construction in IDE Coding Agents

summary.tldr: A new workflow-level jailbreak method for IDE coding agents demonstrates that harmful objectives can be assembled across multiple development stages, bypassing direct chat safety mechanisms and leading to unsafe code generation.
key_points: Workflow-level jailbreak construction assembles harmful objectives across ordinary software development stages, unlike single-prompt attacks.
GitHub Copilot with Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Gemini 3.5 Flash backends were tested.
Models showed near-complete refusal (8/816 successful responses) under direct chat, CSV-read, and single-step code-fix baselines using 204 prompts from Hammurabi's Code, HarmBench, and AdvBench.
Under the full workflow, the same prompts and backends produced 816/816 unsafe teaching-shot completions, confirmed by expert evaluators.
summary.why_it_matters: Current conversational safety benchmarks for coding agents significantly overstate their safety, necessitating new defenses that analyze multi-turn IDE workflows and generated artifacts.

papers.title: Worldscape-MoE: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts World Model for Scalable Heterogeneous Action Control

summary.tldr: Worldscape-MoE is a Mixture-of-Experts world model based on Diffusion Transformers for scalable, unified control across heterogeneous action modalities like locomotion, robotic manipulation, and egocentric hand control.
key_points: Worldscape-MoE uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture built on Diffusion Transformers.
It employs modality-aware control injection to handle diverse action types.
The model utilizes shared and control-specific experts to process heterogeneous action supervision.
A progressive MoE tuning strategy allows for continual extension to new action modalities.
Heterogeneous supervision improves individual control capabilities, as demonstrated in locomotion and hand-control metrics and out-of-distribution generalization.
summary.why_it_matters: This unified framework addresses the scaling bottleneck of fragmented control interfaces in world models, enabling more robust and extensible embodied intelligence.

papers.title: NormWorlds-CF: Solver-Verified Counterfactual Normative Reasoning with Metamorphic-Relation GRPO

summary.tldr: NormWorlds-CF introduces a solver-verified environment for counterfactual normative reasoning, using metamorphic-relation GRPO to improve model competence beyond final answers in executable rule worlds.
key_points: NormWorlds-CF provides a deterministic solver generating final answers, proof/falsification certificates, argument statuses, support sets, and paired-world change labels for supervision.
The benchmark includes 270 root families and 1080 canonical-to-variant pairs for a compact paired-world task, alongside staged SFT diagnostics.
Full-mix training with targeted replay achieves 0.99 accuracy across all tasks, while answer-only SFT yields perfect answer accuracy but zero falsification competence.
Metamorphic-relation GRPO (MR-GRPO) is introduced as a class-conditioned reward for GRPO, giving partial credit for relation families and solver-visible change fields.
MR-GRPO improves held-out relation accuracy and relation-family correctness in Qwen3-1.7B experiments and leads on answer-, support-, and status-change fields in Qwen3-4B validation.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates that verified counterfactual structure can significantly shape post-training of language models, leading to more robust normative reasoning beyond just correct final verdicts.

papers.title: The Remarkable Effectiveness of Providing AI Agents with Natural Language Tools: A Replication Study Validating NLT Performance Across 14 Models

summary.tldr: This study validates Natural Language Tools (NLT) across 14 models, showing it improves tool-calling accuracy by 14.9 percentage points and reduces critical errors by 93% compared to structured methods.
key_points: NLT improves overall tool-calling accuracy by 14.9 percentage points (62.3% vs. 47.4% structured) across 14 models and 8,560 trials.
NLT reduces critical errors by 93% (51 vs. 755 errors) compared to structured tool calling.
NLT benefits are greater for models without native tool calling, reasoning models, and smaller models (+24.0pp to +43.1pp), while frontier models show smaller or reversed advantages.
NLT decreases token usage by 25.2%.
summary.why_it_matters: NLT offers a more reliable and efficient alternative to structured tool calling, particularly for production systems where error reduction and resource optimization are critical.

papers.title: MPSelectTune: Prompt-type Selection for Fine-tuning improves Concept Unlearning in LLMs

summary.tldr: MPSelectTune is a two-stage adversarial approach that improves concept unlearning in LLMs by fine-tuning on the "worst prompt type" for concept prediction, minimizing its concept accuracy.
key_points: MPSelectTune uses a novel adversarial approach with a joint prompt for main task and concept task prediction.
The method fine-tunes using the prompt type with the highest concept accuracy (worst prompt type) to improve average unlearning performance.
MPSelectTune is a two-stage approach that minimizes the concept accuracy of the highest accuracy-prompt type after fine-tuning with a multi-task loss using multiple prompt types.
Experimental results show 2-15% main task accuracy improvements and up to 17% reduction in worst-case concept accuracy compared to recent baselines on four benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more robust way to remove biased or harmful concepts from LLMs, leading to safer and more ethical AI responses across diverse prompt types.

papers.title: Context Graphs for Proactive Enterprise Agents

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Context Graphs for proactive enterprise agents, enabling them to surface relevant information before human queries by modeling entities, relationships, and state transitions.
key_points: Proposes Context Graph, a live relational data structure modeling enterprise entities, relationships, and state transitions over time.
Defines a Delta Detection Engine for continuous state change monitoring, a Proactivity Scorer for ranking insights, and an LLM-powered Surfacing Layer for notifications.
Achieves Precision@5 of 0.83 and reduces mean time to surface from 47 minutes to under 30 seconds in enterprise case studies.
Provides a unified Proactivity Score function and an end-to-end Python implementation using NetworkX and Anthropic Claude API.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables genuine enterprise productivity gains by shifting AI agents from reactive to proactive information delivery.

papers.title: Consistent but Miscalibrated: Evaluating LLM Limitations for Risk Communication in Natural Language

summary.tldr: This paper evaluates nine LLMs' ability to communicate probabilistic information in natural language, finding them consistent but miscalibrated, especially for uncertainty tasks.
key_points: Nine LLMs were evaluated for their ability to verbalize probabilistic information (likelihood and uncertainty) from a two-stage prediction pipeline.
Upstream model predictions were simulated using samples from a Beta distribution parameterized by mode and prior sample size.
Experiments involved six domain contexts, ten temperature settings, and ten repetitions for each LLM.
LLMs demonstrated general consistency but significant miscalibration, performing substantially worse on uncertainty tasks than likelihood tasks.
Providing precomputed summary statistics (mode and prior sample size) reduced contextual sensitivity but did not resolve the underlying miscalibration.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLMs are not reliable zero-shot standalone tools for communicating probabilistic risk, limiting their use as post-hoc explainers of AI outputs.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM Uncertainty in Long-Form Generation Using Deterministic Ground Truth

summary.tldr: A new benchmark, SALT, uses procedurally generated tasks with deterministic ground truth to evaluate LLM uncertainty in long-form generation at fine-grained levels.
key_points: SALT is a benchmark of six procedurally generated tasks with single deterministic long textual ground truths for unit-level evaluation.
Analysis of 50+ LLMs on SALT shows confidence ranking largely fails at atomic resolution but improves at line-level units.
Controlled atom-level interventions reveal error propagation from corrupted prefixes (global context) and bounded degradation from increasing answer-context length.
Reasoning (Chain-of-Thought or internalized) improves accuracy but degrades confidence ranking.
The benchmark enables evaluation of correctness, calibration, and ranking without external judges.
summary.why_it_matters: This research directly impacts risk-critical applications by improving reliable error identification and mitigation in long-form LLM outputs.

papers.title: Unified Backbone Refinement for Diffusion Models via Internal-Latent Analysis

summary.tldr: DUNE is a training-free refinement framework for diffusion models that detects and suppresses abrupt fluctuations in deep internal latents to improve fidelity and reduce hallucinations.
key_points: Abrupt, early-stage fluctuations in deep latents of diffusion models are strongly associated with artifacts.
DUNE detects abrupt deviations in deep low-noise internal latents using a shared EMA-based criterion.
DUNE applies backbone-specific suppression to detector-selected entries.
The detect-suppress principle extends to Transformer-based diffusion models by acting on latents of deep self-attention blocks.
summary.why_it_matters: DUNE offers a training-free method to enhance diffusion model fidelity and reduce hallucinations across various backbones.

papers.title: High-Fidelity One-Step Generative Visuomotor Policy via Recursive Correction, Frequency Consistency, and Contrastive Flow Matching

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a one-step generative visuomotor policy framework using recursive correction, frequency consistency, and contrastive flow matching to achieve high-fidelity, low-latency control.
key_points: Recursive Consistent Action Flow (RCAF) employs recursive correction to mitigate spatial truncation errors and align one-step predictions with refined flow trajectories.
Dual-Timestep Frequency Consistency (DTFC) maintains high-frequency manipulation details via adaptive spectral consistency across flow timesteps.
Contrastive Flow Matching (CFM) disentangles action flows using a margin-based repulsive objective to reduce ambiguity in multimodal manipulation.

The method achieves competitive or superior performance compared to 10-step generative policy baselines with a single forward pass (1 NFE) on RoboTwin, RoboTwin 2.0, Adroit, DexArt, and real-world robot platforms.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables low-latency visuomotor control by reducing inference time from multi-step sampling to a single forward pass while maintaining high fidelity.
